newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE to ban its men from marrying non-Arabs.
newsitem.headline: UAE to ban its men from marrying non-Arabs.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates plans to ban its men from marrying non-Arab women to shield society from the "negative influences of mixed marriages", an official said on Tuesday.

Jamal al-Bah, head of a state-sponsored Marriage Fund, said the draft law "to organise marriages to foreigners" was expected to take effect early next year after cabinet approval and endorsement by President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan.
"The new law will rationalise marriage to foreigners...it is close to a ban," he told Reuters in an interview.

"It will allow marriages from Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nationals because of family links and from fourth-generation relatives in Arab countries," he added. "Otherwise, marriages from all other nationalities will be banned".
The GCC is an economic and political alliance that groups the UAE with Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain and Kuwait.
Oman, Saudi Arabia and Qatar have in recent years imposed similar restrictions on mixed marriages.

Bah said the decision was made after evaluating mixed marriages in the UAE over the past 25 years and their cultural and psychological effects on the couple's children. Sixty percent of all divorces were from mixed marriages, he said.
"This affects their children, they remain scattered, it affects their education and Arabic language."
UAE officials blame high divorce rates in the oil-rich state and a growing number of unmarried women on men taking foreign wives, mainly Asians, to avoid high marriage and dowry costs.
It launched a two-week anti-divorce campaign earlier this month to curb the rising number of failed marriages.
In recent years 36 in every 100 marriages have ended in divorce compared with 10 in every 100 in the 1980s, according to a study by the Labour and Social Affairs Ministry.
Bah, director-general of the fund set up in 1982 by Sheikh Zaid to encourage men to marry local women, had granted up to 11,000 men around 750 million dirhams ($200 million).
This helped reduce the rate of UAE men taking foreign wives to around 21 percent from 40 percent earlier, he said.
Foreigners comprise about 75 percent of the UAE's 2.4 million population.
Bah said in a newspaper interview on Monday the fund was planning to expand its activities by setting up match-making centres across the UAE to promote marriages among nationals.
